subject: gargoyle
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge.
Style: gothic stone carving.

spec.name: Cathedral Gargoyle
spec.description: A hunched gothic stone gargoyle crouched on a weathered cathedral ledge, with bat wings folded up, horned head, fanged open jaw and a curled tail.
spec.layout: A ledge slab (x -0.75..0.75, z -0.7..0.75, y 0..0.2) carries the crouched gargoyle facing +Z. Haunches and hind legs sit at the back (z about -0.25), the torso slopes forward and up to heavy shoulders (y about 0.8, z about 0.15). The arms reach down and forward, with clawed hands gripping the ledge front (z about 0.5). The head is big and jutting, up at y about 1.0 and z about 0.5, with a brow ridge, flat snout, upper and lower jaw with fangs, two curled horns and pointed ears. Bat wings rise from the shoulders and are held half-folded, swept back and up to y 1.3, with bony fingers and a membrane between them. The tail curls from the rump around the left side of the ledge. Every surface is a flat stone colour. Moss sits on upward faces, soot-dark streaks under the ledge, and chipped lighter edges are small parts. Chunky faceted low-poly shapes with sharp chiselled planes. Eyes are small glowing amber parts under a heavy brow.

parts.builds: The cathedral ledge: a chunky slab with a chamfered front lip, corbel blocks underneath, a moulded trim strip and a pointed-arch relief carving on the front face. Includes cracks, chipped corner blocks, moss patches on the top, and soot streaks. Colours: ledge, ledgeTrim, moss, mossDark, stoneSoot, crack. Kept simple relative to the gargoyle.
parts.attaches: Top face at ledgeTop. The feet of the gargoyle (footL, footR, handL and handR claws) rest on it.

parts.builds: Hunched torso as a loft on the pelvis and chest joints, with a ribbed chest, spine ridge of stone spikes, a heavy belly and a pelvis block. Both haunches with thighs, shins and big three-clawed feet gripping the ledge. Surface details: chisel facets, a carved chest emblem, cracks and moss on the back. Colours: stoneMid on top, stoneDark underneath, stoneLight edges, moss, stoneSoot, fang for claws.
parts.attaches: Torso front at neckBase and chest, with shoulders at shoulderL and shoulderR. Hips at hipL and hipR. Rump at tailRoot. Wings root at wingRootL and wingRootR.

parts.builds: Big characterful head: a thick short neck, a skull block with a heavy brow ridge, glowing amber eyes, a flat wide snout with nostrils, a separate upper jaw with fangs and a lower jaw hinged at the jaw joint with an open mouth, a tongue, and chin tusks. Two curled horns, two pointed bat ears, cheek ridges, a stone beard of wedge blades. Colours: stoneMid, stoneLight, stoneDark, horn, fang, eyeGlow, crack, mossDark.
parts.attaches: Neck base at neckBase on the chest. Jaw hinges at jawHinge. The head is centred at headCenter. Nothing sits in front of the face.

parts.builds: Both muscular arms from shoulder balls through elbows to big hands, as chunky tubes with knuckle blocks and three long clawed fingers plus a thumb each, spread and gripping the ledge front. Shoulder pads with spikes and a stone cuff band. Colours: stoneMid, stoneLight, stoneDark, fang for claws, moss on the tops, stoneSoot.
parts.attaches: Shoulders at shoulderL and shoulderR on the torso. Hands rest on the ledge at wristL and wristR.

parts.builds: Two bat wings, mirrored, rooted at wingRootL and wingRootR: a thick arm bone, then a wrist with a thumb claw and three long finger bones fanned, with scalloped membranes between them in membrane colour, with stone-crack lines and rivet-like studs along the bones. Plus the tail: a tapering swept tube from tailRoot curling round the left of the ledge, ending in a spade-shaped tip with a spike ridge. Colours: wingBone, membrane, stoneDark, stoneLight, stoneMid, moss on the upper bone edges.
parts.attaches: Wing roots at wingRootL and wingRootR on the shoulders. Tail begins at tailRoot at the rump.

calls.reasoning:
I'm working out the arm joint positions for the shoulder, elbow, and wrist on each side, making sure the hands land on top of the ledge at the right height.

For construction, I'll build each arm as two capsule sweeps (upper arm and forearm) rigged to their respective joints, giving them a faceted six-sided cross-section with tapering radii so they look rounded but low-poly at the joints.

Now I'm working out the hand geometry: a palm box at the wrist, knuckle blocks, and three two-segment fingers plus a thumb, positioned so they curl forward and down from the wrist to grip over the ledge's front edge with claws resting on its top surface.

Positioning the thumb on the inner side toward center, attaching claws via spike primitives on the handL bone, and considering whether to add extra joints for the fingers or keep them rigid on the wrist bone.

Adding digit chains with two joints per finger (proximal and distal) for each of four fingers across both hands, naming them consistently and giving them a "digit" role, then setting up the shoulder as a sphere joint.

Moving on to shoulder details like a flattened dodecahedron pad with spikes and moss blobs, a cuff band near the wrist using an angled cylinder shape, elbow spurs and knuckle balls, and muscle bulges defined through varying sweep radii for the forearm and upper arm plus bicep ellipsoids.

I'm mapping left/right sides by naming joints with L/R suffixes and aligning cylinders along the arm direction using the vector from shoulder to elbow. I'm setting up a lerp helper for positioning along segments and assigning palette colors like stoneMid and stoneLight to the various shoulder spikes and pad elements.

Writing capsule bone code...

Still working out shoulder anatomy...

Adding a moss patch on the pad and a biceps bulge with ridge detailing along the upper arm, sized and angled to follow the limb direction.

Now I'm detailing the elbow with a ball joint and a backward-pointing spur spike, then building the forearm with a bulge near the elbow and a hexagonal cuff with dark trim rings further down.

I'm adding small dark studs around the cuff and mossy, flattened details on top of the arm with soot streaks underneath, then shaping the hand with a palm box and bevel plate, plus a wrist ball, working out their precise positions relative to the wrist joint.

Now I'm positioning the three fingers, fanning them outward from the palm with lateral offsets and figuring out knuckle placement relative to the palm center.

I'm recalculating the palm depth and compressing the finger joint positions so they fit within the bounding box, adjusting knuckle, mid, and tip coordinates so the pointing-down posture stays inside the ledge, and scaling the middle finger slightly longer than the others.

Now I'm defining the finger geometry with narrower radius and fewer sides, then adding a curved claw spike at the distal tip using a base-to-tip spike call with small radius. For the skeleton, I'm setting up proximal and distal joint bones aimed between the knuckle, mid, and tip points, parenting them to the hand and attaching the claw bone to the distal segment.

For the thumb, I'm positioning its base, mid, and tip points on the inner side of the wrist (mirrored for left vs right), adding its own claw tip, and chaining its joints under an "armsThumb" role, using aim-based joint orientation via Vector3 targets. I'm also adding a knuckle ridge detail with small icosphere shapes.

Now I'm adding smaller finger details—tiny stone chips, knuckle spikes, moss patches on the palm—and tallying up the full part count per side: shoulder ball and pad with spikes and moss, cracks, upper arm pieces, elbow components, forearm with cuff studs and soot, wrist and palm elements, and knuckle sets.

Totaling roughly 58 pieces per side gives about 116 overall, comfortably under the 150 limit. Mirroring both sides, I'm working out the correct rotation signs for the pad so the outer edge tilts downward correctly depending on whether it's the left or right side, using degree-based rotation around the z-axis.

I'm setting up a part helper that wraps the module's part-creation function with position and bone attachment, plus spike and ellipsoid helpers for limb segments that take direction vectors and scale factors for shaping.

I'm working out how to define the buildTorsoAndLegs function and whether the Ctx type should come from the existing module or be declared locally, since this is replacing the whole module file.

Now I'm mapping out the joint positions for the legs—hip, knee, foot—and figuring out how to build thigh and shin segments as sweeps or lofts along these bone positions, then moving on to the torso loft from pelvis to chest to neck base.

Adding torso loft stations...

I'll settle on sides:8 with smooth:false, and use sectors to countershade the belly darker underneath, since loft is documented as a shorthand for sweep and should forward those options. Then I plan to add surface detail with scatter placement on the torso.

For the spine ridge, I'll walk along the torso path placing decreasing-size spikes oriented outward using the sweep's frame at each point, nudging each spike's base slightly to embed into the curved surface.

For ribs, I'm thinking of looping thin rings around the chest at several points along the torso axis, using a center point and direction rather than a chain, since the chest surface needs a plane passing through that point facing the bone's direction.

I need to restrict the rib loops to only the lower front half by slicing the angle range, raising them slightly as ridges with a light/dark stone coloring, though I'm wary loops could fail if the plane misses the torso surface or accidentally cut through limbs since those aren't part of this surface.

Now I'm adding a chest emblem: casting a ray from the front toward the torso to find where it hits, then placing a small extruded shield shape with a cross or fleur motif at that point, oriented so its thickness extrudes outward from the chest surface.

Now I'm designing the chest emblem attached to the chest bone—a shield outline with an inner gothic arch and three small spheres arranged like a trefoil, built from extruded diamond shapes. I'm figuring out where to cast the ray for the chest surface, accounting for the head and torso positions so the emblem sits centered below the neck, away from the arms.

For the back, I'm scattering flattened moss clusters onto upward-facing surfaces, using filtered raycast hits and sticking scaled-down icosahedron shapes with partial embedding to create a mossy texture.

I'm also adding thin dark crack lines using slim boxes stuck onto the surface with random spin, plus planning lighter chisel-facet details for texture variation.

Now I'm shaping the pelvis and belly structure, placing a tilted box for the pelvis block and considering sphere-based pads for the belly to give the body more volume and definition.

Working through leg placement next, positioning hip joints and sculpting thigh forms with scaled spheres and sweeps from hip to knee.

Continuing down the leg, I'm placing the knee as a small faceted sphere, then working out the shin geometry to give a digitigrade, crouched stance with the knee forward and the hock angled back toward the foot.

Still placing the foot geometry, now sizing the foot block and adding three clawed toes with spike tips, keeping the toe curves resting flush on the ledge surface at y≈0.22.

Moving to the legs, I'm setting up a bone hierarchy with hip, knee, and foot joints mirrored across left and right sides, then positioning the thigh segment horizontally from hip to knee with a thick haunch radius tapering toward the knee.

Working through the chain of torso stations from pelvis to shoulder, I realize the end cap dome at the final station pushes well past the box edge into head territory, so I need to shrink that station or pick a flatter cap style instead.

Adding a spine bone loft between pelvis and chest joints, and considering optional shoulder hump or scapula details that might get covered by the arms anyway. Now I'm shaping a flattened belly sphere mounted on the pelvis bone for added bulk.

Still defining foot geometry...

Now I'm skipping extra toe joints and moving to the haunch area: building a thigh muscle shape between hip and knee with muted stone tones, adding a bone joint, a darker underside, and a tapered thigh tube. Adding inner arch details...

Adding chip and soot scatter logic...

Writing leg geometry loop...

Positioning the haunch ellipsoid against the hip offset, checking its extents overlap sensibly with the torso and thigh. Now thinking through coloring details—stone tones for the haunch and thigh chips, claw color for toe tips—and considering whether small moss sticks belong on the foot or thigh surfaces.

Working out how to attach moss patches and shoulder blade plates using surface-around-center lookups with specific azimuth and elevation angles, guarding against null hits when the sweep misses.

Still writing creature detail code...

I should wrap the rib loop in a try/catch in case the plane direction fails near the shoulder. Skipping the neck collar band since that belongs to the head part, but I'll add a belly sphere. Adding thigh studs...

I'm thinking through how to handle the ledge part without explicit joints—since parts default to the nearest joint by position, I need to make sure that works correctly for a static piece, or else explicitly assign it a bone to be safe.

For attachment, I'll tie the ledge to the pelvis joint since that's the root, keeping it rigid against any pose and avoiding it splitting across joints if someone animates the model. For materials I'll stick to the existing palette colors with maybe a light stone accent for texture chips.

Working out the geometry for the chamfer strip trim...
